titles: 0.72 Sounds Small. It Turns 100 Grandparents Into 4 Great-Grandkids
South Korea Didn't Just Age — It Broke Population Math (51.8M → 36M)
You Think This Is a Korea Problem. Every Country on This Chart Is Behind It
primary_title: 0.72 Sounds Small. It Turns 100 Grandparents Into 4 Great-Grandkids
description:
South Korea's fertility rate is 0.72, and that one decimal turns 100 grandparents into fewer than 5 great-grandchildren in three generations — a 95% contraction with no war, no famine, no plague. Below replacement, demography stops behaving like a slow decline and starts behaving like reverse compound interest, and Korea is simply the first country to arrive.

We run the arithmetic on screen, invert Korea's population pyramid in real time, and then pull back to the chart that matters: Japan, Italy, Spain, China, and the US running the identical descent, 15 to 40 years behind the same line.

CHAPTERS
00:00 — Introduction & The Intuition Trap
01:24 — The Historical Inflection Point
03:05 — The Data Divergence
04:46 — The 2030 Horizon & Conclusion

KEY DATA TAKEAWAYS
• South Korea's total fertility rate fell from 4.53 (1970) to 0.72 (2023), with a slight rebound to roughly 0.75 in 2024 — against a replacement rate of 2.1. Seoul sits near 0.55. In 2018 Korea became the first nation in peacetime history to fall below 1.0.
• Statistics Korea's medium-variant projection takes the population from its 51.8M peak to roughly 36M by 2072, cuts the working-age cohort close to half, and pushes median age from about 45 into the low 60s — with the worker-to-retiree ratio sliding from roughly 5:1 toward 1:1.
• Korea is the front of the curve, not an outlier: Japan crossed 1.3 in 2005, Italy hit a record-low ~1.18 in 2024, China fell to roughly 1.0–1.1 as annual births halved from 18.8M (2016) to about 9.5M (2024), and the US recorded a record-low ~1.6.

METHODOLOGY NOTE
The 100-person model uses a generational multiplier of TFR ÷ 2 (0.72 ÷ 2 = 0.36 per person, i.e. 100 grandparents → 36 → 13 → 4.7). It is a deliberately simplified illustration of cohort arithmetic: it holds fertility constant, and excludes mortality, net migration, the ~1.05 male-to-female birth ratio, and changes in generational timing. Real projections, including Statistics Korea's, model all of these and are shown separately wherever a projected figure appears. Generation length is treated as roughly 30 years for the 2025 / 2055 / 2085 / 2115 timeline. Figures for 2024 are provisional and subject to revision.
